newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee council members now to meet July 29.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee council members now to meet July 29.

text.p: A preparatory meeting for the next session of Brazil's coffee council, the CPDC, has been postponed again and will now be held on July 29, said the head of the growers' National Coffee Council (CNC).
The meeting which has already been re-scheduled twice, had been expected to take place on July 22.
The council, which unites representatives from the public and private sectors, is to hold its next formal session in Santos but so far no date has been set.
Topics to be discussed by the council include stock financing for producers, said the CNC's Gilson Ximenes.
A proposal put to the council earlier this year suggested that 150 million reais should be made available to producers through to September.
"I want 150 million reais but at the very least 100 million reais," Ximenes said.
Members are also expected to discuss ways of helping the domestic soluble coffee industry which claims to be losing competitiveness due to higher raw material costs than in other countries.
